original_question: Calculate the cost of goods sold and ending inventory using the FIFO method when a business purchases 100 units at Tk. 20 per unit and subsequently purchases another 80 units at Tk. 25 per unit. The business sells 120 units during the accounting period.

transformations.Understand: Explain why the FIFO method assigns the cost of the earliest purchased units to the 120 units sold before assigning costs to the remaining inventory.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how the purchase sequence of 100 units at Tk. 20 and 80 units at Tk. 25 determines the cost layers used for the 120 units sold and the units remaining in inventory.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether the reported cost of goods sold of Tk. 2,500 and ending inventory of Tk. 1,500 are consistent with the FIFO method and the stated purchases and sales. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop an inventory-valuation comparison for the purchases of 100 units at Tk. 20 and 80 units at Tk. 25 and the sale of 120 units, showing cost of goods sold and ending inventory under FIFO and a second method of your choice, and recommend one for reporting.

original_question: Determine the first-order partial derivatives of the function f(x,y)=3x^2y+2xy^2-5y with respect to x and y.

transformations.Remember: State the definition of a first-order partial derivative and explain which variable is held constant when differentiating with respect to the other variable.
transformations.Understand: Explain how partial differentiation treats the other independent variable as constant when differentiating f(x,y)=3x^2y+2xy^2-5y.
transformations.Analyze: Examine the individual terms 3x^2y, 2xy^2, and -5y to distinguish their contributions to the partial derivatives with respect to x and y.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether the proposed derivatives f_x=6xy+2y^2 and f_y=3x^2+4xy-5 are mathematically correct for the stated function. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Construct the equation of the tangent plane to f(x,y)=3x^2y+2xy^2-5y at a point of your choice using its first-order partial derivatives.

original_question: Explain how the interlacement of warp and weft yarns produces the structure of a plain weave and how its alternating over-one and under-one pattern affects fabric characteristics.

transformations.Remember: Define plain weave and identify warp and weft yarns as the two yarn systems involved in its construction.
transformations.Apply: Determine the interlacement sequence for a plain weave in which each warp yarn passes over one weft yarn and under the next successive weft yarn.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how the alternating over-one and under-one interlacement creates the structural characteristics of plain-weave fabric.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether a proposed weave pattern in which each warp yarn passes over two consecutive weft yarns and under the next two is consistent with the defining interlacement pattern of plain weave. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a woven structure derived from plain weave, such as a rib weave, and draw its interlacement diagram, showing how its warp and weft interlacement differs from the one-over, one-under structure.

original_question: Determine the sequence of states in a 4-bit Johnson counter starting from 0000, where the complemented output of the last flip-flop is fed back to the input of the first flip-flop and the register shifts one position on each clock pulse.

transformations.Remember: Define a Johnson counter and identify the feedback connection that distinguishes it from a conventional ring counter.
transformations.Understand: Explain how complemented feedback and successive shifting produce the state sequence of a 4-bit Johnson counter.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how the complemented output of the last flip-flop affects the next state of the first flip-flop and how this relationship propagates through the four-bit register.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether the proposed sequence 0000 →1000 →1100 →1110 →1111 →0111 →0011 →0001 →0000 follows the stated feedback and shifting conditions. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design decoding logic for the stated 4-bit Johnson counter that generates an output pulse in a chosen state, specifying the state sequence and the two-bit condition that identifies that state.

original_question: Analyze how content validity, construct validity, and criterion-related validity contribute to determining whether a university examination measures the intended learning outcomes.

transformations.Remember: Define content validity, construct validity, and criterion-related validity in educational assessment.
transformations.Understand: Explain how the three forms of validity provide different perspectives on whether a university examination measures its intended learning outcomes.
transformations.Apply: Classify the following assessment concerns: insufficient representation of course topics, failure to measure the intended cognitive ability, and weak agreement with an established external measure, according to content, construct, and criterion-related validity respectively.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether an examination can be considered adequately valid when it covers the course syllabus but fails to measure the intended higher-order cognitive skills. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a validity-review framework for a university examination that examines content representation, measurement of intended constructs, and relationships with relevant external criteria.

original_question: Analyze how the extract, transform, and load (ETL) process prepares data from operational systems for storage in a data warehouse, considering data extraction, format standardization, and loading into the target repository.

transformations.Remember: Expand ETL and identify extraction, transformation, and loading as its three principal stages.
transformations.Understand: Explain how extracting data, standardizing its format, and loading it into a target repository prepare operational data for analytical use in a data warehouse.
transformations.Apply: Arrange the following ETL activities in their correct sequence: standardizing extracted data formats, retrieving data from operational systems, and loading the transformed data into the target warehouse.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether loading operational data directly into a data warehouse without standardizing inconsistent formats adequately satisfies the stated ETL preparation requirements. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop an ETL workflow for the stated data-warehouse context, showing how operational data is extracted, standardized, and loaded into the target repository.

original_question: Explain how compressional forces deform originally horizontal rock layers into anticlines and synclines, distinguishing the geometric characteristics of the two fold types.

transformations.Remember: Define anticlines and synclines and identify the characteristic arrangement of rock layers in each fold type.
transformations.Apply: Classify an upward-arched rock-layer structure as an anticline and a downward-trough-shaped structure as a syncline.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how compressional deformation changes the orientation of originally horizontal rock layers to produce the contrasting geometries of anticlines and synclines.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether describing a syncline as an upward-arched fold is consistent with the geometric distinction between anticlines and synclines. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a geological model of a region in which compression produced an anticline and a syncline that were later eroded, predicting the surface pattern of rock ages across the folds.

original_question: Calculate a patient's net fluid balance over 24 hours when oral intake is 1,200 mL, intravenous intake is 800 mL, urine output is 1,500 mL, and other measured fluid losses are 200 mL.

transformations.Remember: Define fluid intake, fluid output, and net fluid balance, and state the relationship used to calculate net fluid balance.
transformations.Understand: Explain how oral and intravenous intake are compared with urine output and other measured losses when determining a patient's net fluid balance.
transformations.Analyze: Examine the contribution of oral intake, intravenous intake, urine output, and other measured losses to the patient's overall fluid balance during the 24-hour period.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether a reported net fluid balance of +300 mL is consistent with the stated intake and output measurements. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a fluid-management plan for the patient's next 24 hours, based on the previous 24 hours' 1,200 mL oral intake, 800 mL intravenous intake, 1,500 mL urine output, and 200 mL other measured losses, specifying intake targets that achieve a chosen net balance.

original_question: Analyze how bilateral negotiations, multilateral diplomacy, economic sanctions, and diplomatic mediation serve as instruments for pursuing a state's foreign-policy objectives.

transformations.Remember: Identify bilateral negotiations, multilateral diplomacy, economic sanctions, and diplomatic mediation as instruments of foreign policy.
transformations.Understand: Explain how the four stated diplomatic instruments can be used to pursue a state's foreign-policy objectives through different forms of international engagement or pressure.
transformations.Apply: Classify a state's direct negotiation with another government, participation in a multinational diplomatic forum, imposition of trade restrictions, and facilitation of dialogue between two disputing states according to the four stated instruments.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether economic sanctions alone are necessarily sufficient to achieve a state's foreign-policy objectives, considering the distinct functions of bilateral negotiations, multilateral diplomacy, and diplomatic mediation. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a foreign-policy instrument framework showing how bilateral negotiations, multilateral diplomacy, economic sanctions, and diplomatic mediation can be organized in pursuit of a state's objectives.

original_question: Interpret the stress–strain behaviour of a ductile material by identifying the proportional limit, yield point, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture point on its tensile-test curve.

transformations.Remember: Define proportional limit, yield point, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture point on a ductile material's stress–strain curve.
transformations.Apply: Identify the proportional limit, yield point, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture point on a labelled tensile-test curve of a ductile material.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how the material's mechanical response changes between the proportional limit, yield point, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture point.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether a description that identifies the fracture point as the location of maximum engineering stress is consistent with the distinction between ultimate tensile strength and fracture. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a tensile-test reporting specification for a ductile material that states how the proportional limit, yield point, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture point will be determined from the recorded curve and how each will be reported.

topic: Database Systems: Database Recovery with Checkpoints
original_question: Analyze how checkpointing reduces database recovery time after a system failure in a transaction-processing system, considering the role of completed transactions, log records, and the most recent checkpoint.

transformations.Remember: Define a database checkpoint and identify its purpose in transaction recovery.
transformations.Understand: Explain how a checkpoint helps a database recovery system avoid processing the entire transaction log from the beginning after a system failure.
transformations.Apply: Determine the starting point for log-based recovery when a database has checkpoints at log positions 100, 200, and 300 and a failure occurs after log position 350.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether beginning recovery from log position 100 is necessary when the most recent completed checkpoint is at position 300 and the failure occurs at position 350. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a conceptual recovery workflow showing how a database uses the most recent checkpoint and subsequent log records to recover after a system failure.

original_question: Calculate the generated electromotive force per phase of a synchronous generator when the flux per pole is 0.05 Wb, the frequency is 50 Hz, the number of series turns per phase is 100, and the winding factor is 0.9. Use E=4.44K_wfΦT.

transformations.Remember: State the generated-emf equation for a synchronous generator and identify the flux per pole, frequency, number of series turns, and winding factor.
transformations.Understand: Explain how magnetic flux, frequency, number of series turns, and winding factor influence the generated emf per phase.
transformations.Analyze: Examine the individual contributions of K_w=0.9, f=50Hz, Φ=0.05Wb, and T=100 to the generated-emf expression.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether a reported generated emf of 999 V per phase is consistent with the stated synchronous-generator equation and parameters. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a winding modification for the synchronous generator with a flux per pole of 0.05 Wb, frequency of 50 Hz, 100 series turns per phase, and winding factor of 0.9 that produces a chosen target emf per phase, determining the required number of turns using E=4.44K_wfΦT.

original_question: Explain how the chloride limit test detects chloride impurities in a pharmaceutical substance through the formation of silver chloride turbidity and comparison with a standard chloride solution.

transformations.Remember: Identify silver nitrate as the reagent used to produce silver chloride turbidity in the chloride limit test.
transformations.Apply: Interpret a test result in which the turbidity produced by a pharmaceutical sample is greater than that of its standard chloride solution, using the stated comparison principle.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how the formation and relative intensity of silver chloride turbidity provide evidence about chloride impurities in the sample.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether a pharmaceutical sample satisfies the chloride limit-test comparison when its turbidity is visibly greater than that of the standard solution. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a training worksheet for analysts performing the chloride limit test that guides them through the sample reaction, standard comparison, turbidity observation, and result interpretation, including checks for common errors.

original_question: Analyze how the marginal propensity to consume influences the value of the simple expenditure multiplier and the resulting change in equilibrium income.

transformations.Remember: State the simple expenditure multiplier equation k=1/(1-MPC) and define the marginal propensity to consume.
transformations.Understand: Explain why a higher marginal propensity to consume produces a larger simple expenditure multiplier.
transformations.Apply: Calculate the simple expenditure multiplier when the marginal propensity to consume is 0.8, using k=1/(1-MPC).
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether a multiplier of 5 is consistent with a marginal propensity to consume of 0.8 under the simple expenditure multiplier model. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a fiscal-policy scenario that uses the relationship between the marginal propensity to consume and the simple expenditure multiplier to achieve a chosen change in equilibrium income, specifying the assumed marginal propensity to consume and the required change in autonomous spending.

original_question: Analyze how flat, pitched, and curved roof systems differ in structural form, rainwater drainage, and suitability for different building requirements.

transformations.Remember: Identify flat, pitched, and curved roofs as three roof-system types and state one characteristic structural form of each.
transformations.Understand: Explain how the geometric form of flat, pitched, and curved roofs influences rainwater drainage and their architectural applications.
transformations.Apply: Classify a roof with two inclined surfaces meeting at a ridge as a pitched roof and a roof with a continuously curved surface as a curved roof.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether a flat roof is an appropriate choice when rapid rainwater drainage is the principal requirement, comparing its form with pitched and curved alternatives. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a comparative roof-system selection framework that connects flat, pitched, and curved roof forms with structural characteristics, drainage requirements, and building needs.

original_question: Analyze how distance-vector routing updates routing tables when router A initially has a cost of 2 to router B and a cost of 7 to router C, while router B advertises a cost of 3 to router C. Assume the link between A and B is bidirectional and has the same cost in both directions.

transformations.Remember: Define distance-vector routing and identify the role of advertised destination costs in routing-table updates.
transformations.Understand: Explain how router A uses the cost to router B and B's advertised cost to router C to determine an alternative route to C.
transformations.Apply: Calculate the alternative cost from router A to router C through router B using the stated link costs of 2 and 3, and compare it with the direct cost of 7.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether router A should replace its direct route to router C with the route through B, using the stated costs and the shortest-path decision rule. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a split-horizon rule for router A's distance-vector updates in the stated network, and show how it changes the routing information A advertises to B about its route to C.

original_question: Calculate the labour efficiency variance when the standard labour time is 4 hours per unit, actual production is 100 units, actual labour time is 450 hours, and the standard labour rate is Tk. 200 per hour. Use the formula (Standard Hours-Actual Hours)×Standard Rate.

transformations.Remember: State the labour efficiency variance formula and define standard hours, actual hours, and standard labour rate.
transformations.Understand: Explain how differences between the standard hours allowed for actual production and the actual hours worked determine labour efficiency variance.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how the standard time of 4 hours per unit, actual output of 100 units, actual time of 450 hours, and standard rate of Tk. 200 per hour contribute to the variance.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether a reported labour efficiency variance of Tk. 10,000 adverse is consistent with the stated production data and variance formula. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a labour-efficiency improvement plan for the production period with a standard of 4 hours per unit, 100 units produced, 450 actual labour hours, and a standard rate of Tk. 200 per hour, specifying the target labour hours and the resulting variance after improvement.

original_question: Explain how primary and secondary ecological succession differ in their starting conditions, soil availability, and development of biological communities.

transformations.Remember: Define primary and secondary ecological succession and identify the role of soil in distinguishing their starting conditions.
transformations.Apply: Classify vegetation establishment on newly exposed bare rock as primary succession and vegetation recovery after a forest fire where soil remains as secondary succession.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how initial substrate conditions and soil availability influence the development of biological communities during primary and secondary succession.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether describing vegetation recovery after a forest fire as primary succession is consistent with the presence of pre-existing soil. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a long-term field study comparing primary and secondary succession at two sites, specifying how the sites are selected by their starting conditions and soil availability and which community-development measures are recorded.

original_question: Determine whether the undirected graph G=(V,E), where V={A,B,C,D,E} and E={{A,B},{B,C},{C,D},{D,E}}, is connected by examining whether a path exists between every pair of vertices.

transformations.Remember: Define a connected undirected graph and state the condition that must hold between every pair of vertices.
transformations.Understand: Explain how the existence of paths between vertices determines whether an undirected graph is connected.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how the edges {A,B}, {B,C}, {C,D}, and {D,E} link the five vertices into a single component.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether the claim that the stated graph has two connected components is consistent with its vertex and edge sets. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design the minimum set of additional edges that would keep the graph with V={A,B,C,D,E} and E={{A,B},{B,C},{C,D},{D,E}} connected after the removal of any single edge, and show the resulting graph.

topic: Systems Analysis and Design: Feasibility Study
original_question: Analyze how technical, economic, operational, and schedule feasibility influence the decision to develop a proposed university student-information system.

transformations.Remember: Identify technical, economic, operational, and schedule feasibility as the four feasibility dimensions considered in the proposed student-information system.
transformations.Understand: Explain how each feasibility dimension addresses a different concern when determining whether the proposed university system can be developed and implemented.
transformations.Apply: Classify the following project concerns according to the four feasibility dimensions: availability of suitable computing infrastructure, affordability of development costs, staff willingness to use the system, and ability to complete development within the planned deadline.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether a proposed student-information system should proceed when suitable infrastructure is available and staff are willing to use it, but the development cost exceeds the approved budget and the project cannot meet its planned deadline. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a feasibility-assessment framework for the proposed student-information system, showing how technical, economic, operational, and schedule considerations contribute to the development decision.

topic: Geotechnical Engineering: Bearing Capacity of Shallow Foundations
original_question: Explain how soil cohesion, soil unit weight, foundation width, and foundation depth influence the ultimate bearing capacity of a shallow foundation.

transformations.Remember: Identify soil cohesion, soil unit weight, foundation width, and foundation depth as parameters influencing the ultimate bearing capacity of a shallow foundation.
transformations.Apply: Identify which of the four stated parameters represents the foundation's horizontal dimension and which represents its vertical embedment below ground level.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how soil strength characteristics and foundation geometry contribute separately to the ultimate bearing capacity of a shallow foundation.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether increasing foundation width alone guarantees an increase in bearing capacity when soil properties and foundation depth are not considered. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Develop a design procedure for selecting the width and depth of a shallow foundation that accounts for soil cohesion, soil unit weight, foundation width, and foundation depth to achieve a required bearing capacity.

original_question: Analyze how the phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, central executive, and episodic buffer contribute to information processing in the working-memory model.

transformations.Remember: Identify the phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, central executive, and episodic buffer as components of the working-memory model.
transformations.Understand: Explain the distinct functions of the four working-memory components in maintaining and processing information.
transformations.Apply: Classify temporary verbal rehearsal, temporary visual-spatial representation, coordination of attentional resources, and integration of information from different sources according to the four components of working memory.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether a description of the central executive as the component responsible only for storing visual information accurately represents its function in the working-memory model. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a classroom task that deliberately engages each of the four working-memory components, specifying which part of the task loads each component and how the components integrate the information.

original_question: Calculate the decimal reduction time (D-value) when a microbial population decreases from 10^6 to 10^3 cells under constant processing conditions over 6 minutes. Assume logarithmic linear inactivation.

transformations.Remember: Define the decimal reduction time (D-value) and state what a one-logarithm reduction represents in microbial population.
transformations.Understand: Explain how a reduction from 10^6 to 10^3 cells over 6 minutes represents successive decimal reductions under logarithmic linear inactivation.
transformations.Analyze: Examine the initial population of 10^6, final population of 10^3, and processing time of 6 minutes to determine the number of decimal reductions represented by the treatment.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether a reported D-value of 2 minutes is consistent with the stated microbial reduction and processing time. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a thermal process for the microbial population that decreases from 10^6 to 10^3 cells in 6 minutes under constant processing conditions that achieves a chosen target log reduction, specifying the required processing time, assuming log-linear inactivation.

original_question: Evaluate the suitability of performance-based budgeting for a public health department that allocates funds to vaccination services, using service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and achievement of annual vaccination targets as performance indicators.

transformations.Remember: Define performance-based budgeting and identify service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and annual target achievement as performance indicators.
transformations.Understand: Explain how linking budget allocations to service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and annual vaccination targets can connect public expenditure with service performance.
transformations.Apply: Classify service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and annual vaccination target achievement according to whether each measures service reach, expenditure efficiency, or target attainment.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how the three stated indicators provide different information about the performance of vaccination services funded by the public health department.
transformations.Create: Develop a performance-based budget framework for the vaccination service, linking funding decisions to service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and annual target achievement.

topic: Phonetics: Place and Manner of Articulation
original_question: Classify the English consonant sounds /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, and /s/ according to their place and manner of articulation.

transformations.Remember: Define place of articulation and manner of articulation in the classification of consonant sounds.
transformations.Understand: Explain how the location and type of constriction in the vocal tract distinguish the consonant sounds /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, and /s/.
transformations.Analyze: Examine the articulatory features of /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, and /s/ to distinguish differences in their places and manners of articulation.
transformations.Evaluate: Verify whether the classification of /f/ as a bilabial stop and /k/ as a velar stop is consistent with their articulatory characteristics. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a minimal-pair listening exercise using /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, and /s/ that contrasts their place and manner of articulation, specifying the word pairs and the articulatory feature each pair tests.

original_question: Compare write-through and write-back cache policies in terms of when modified data is transferred to main memory, memory traffic, and the handling of modified cache blocks.

transformations.Remember: Define write-through and write-back cache policies and identify when each policy transfers modified data to main memory.
transformations.Apply: Determine when main memory is updated under each policy after a processor modifies a cached data block.
transformations.Analyze: Examine how immediate memory updates in write-through caching and deferred updates in write-back caching affect memory traffic and the management of modified cache blocks.
transformations.Evaluate: Assess whether write-back caching is preferable to write-through caching when reducing main-memory traffic is the primary design objective, while accounting for the need to track modified cache blocks. Justify your judgement with explicit reference to the criteria used.
transformations.Create: Design a hybrid cache-write scheme that uses write-back for most blocks but writes through selected blocks, specifying the selection rule and the sequence of operations after a processor modifies a cached block.
